title: Auxiliary curve over the NIST P-192 prime with a rational point of order 2^48 (PKM isogeny-tower factor base, t = 48)
status_note: Blocked on the wide-field tower builder and the 192-bit field backend (both in progress, not yet pushed) and on PR #1889. Runs as cairn lab tasks with the native checker deciding `found` (first_success); posting it as a cairn objective is the upgrade path once cairn can pin a native checker. Recommended gate: run only after lead 1 (XP-20261015-pkm-m3-n21-m4-n20) gives a bounded F4 solving degree, or run it explicitly as an infrastructure/feasibility measurement.
blocked_on: branch:claude/isogeny-tower-wide wide-field isogeny-tower builder lane, in progress (not yet pushed); provides the solver binary and the 2-Sylow halving filter
branch:claude/fp-backend Stage 0 192-bit prime-field backend, in progress (not yet pushed); its measured Legendre/sqrt cost fixes the per-trial cost below
pr:1889 the measured small-field tower and auxiliary-curve search (open, unmerged)

notes: research/pkm_isogeny_tower_ecbench_20261015/README.md on branch claude/leads-isogeny-tower (panel 3: curves tried / 2^t, pooled C = 1.05 over 224 builds, t = 8..14; projection to P-192 size)

question: How many auxiliary curves over the NIST P-192 prime must be drawn, and at what wall cost per draw, before one has a rational point of order 2^48, using a curve family that forces k bits of 2-power torsion and a halving filter that rejects most draws after O(1) square roots?
decision_value: This run prices the construction of a P-192-size isogeny-tower factor base; it does not by itself say anything about P-192 security. The base is useful only if the tower's F4 solving degree stays bounded as the tower grows (encyclopedia §8 lead 1), which is unresolved and trending negative (D rises at m = 2, N = 20). If lead 1 comes back bounded, a curve found here is the input the relation phase needs and the measured trials-per-success fixes the construction's share of the cost; if lead 1 stays unbounded, this run only measures a feasibility constant and should be scheduled as infrastructure work, not as attack evidence. A failure to find a curve within the seed space is a bounded negative result about this family and filter, not about the tower.

resources.notes: Expected total for the Z/2 x Z/2 family (k = 2) at 2 us per draw: 2^46 draws ~ 39,000 core-hours ~ 4.5 core-years; range 9,800 core-hours (k = 4, 2 us) to 391,000 core-hours (k = 2, 20 us), i.e. 1.1-45 core-years. Embarrassingly parallel: wall time is core-hours / cores. Per shard (2^32 draws, one core): 8,590-85,900 s = 2.4-23.9 h at 2-20 us per draw. Derivation in README.md. The per-draw cost is a placeholder until claude/fp-backend measures a 192-bit Legendre symbol and square root.

params.seed_meaning: seed s deterministically derives one curve draw (a, b) of the family; the derivation is fixed in PROTOCOL.md before the card leaves blocked

outputs.result_schema: the solver's result JSON: {a, b, Q: [x, y], t, seed, draws, cpu_seconds}, frozen in PROTOCOL.md

cairn.notes: One lab task per seed range; stop rule first_success (backlog/README.md): before each claim a runner checks `backlog cairn-found <ID> --lab DIR` (exit 3 = stop); a run that finds a curve writes {out}/found/artifact.json, which `cairn lab exec --publish runs/<ID>/shard-<k>` publishes, and the runner, still holding the lease, records it with `backlog cairn-found <ID> --lab DIR --lab-path runs/<ID>/shard-<k>/found/artifact.json --claim C --holder H --identity I --checker-bin <pinned build>/backlog_check_aux2t` (the checker decides on the lab copy). Re-claim every 2 h (ttl 6 h). Resumable from checkpoint.json, so preemptible. Upgrade path: a cairn objective once cairn can pin a native checker (problems/cairn-certificate-checker-python-only.md).

env.name: crypto-aux-search
env.recipe: A rust:1.98 image built at the builder lane merge commit with `cargo build --release --bin pkm-aux-search --bin backlog_check_aux2t`, imported with `cairn lab env import crypto-aux-search-<sha> --docker <image>`

p.description: decimal or 0x-hex; must be the NIST P-192 prime

artifact_schema.checks: t = 48 (the checker is run with --expect-t 48); p is the NIST P-192 prime; 4a^3 + 27b^2 != 0 mod p; Q on y^2 = x^3 + ax + b; [2^47]Q != O and [2^48]Q = O; exit 0 accept, 1 reject, 2 bad input

funding.rationale: Lowest of the four: gated on lead 1 (the base only matters if the F4 solving degree is bounded), and 1-45 core-years of construction that by itself says nothing about P-192 security.
